concerns.text: FR-009 introduces a full a‑priori power analysis targeting f² ≥ 0.15 with power ≥ 0.80. The original idea did not request any power‑analysis step; it only called for bootstrapping to assess robustness. Adding this requirement expands the research scope beyond the stated question.

FR-006 mandates a hard 6‑hour CI timeout and graceful partial exit. The idea never mentioned CI‑environment limits or fallback execution; this is an engineering constraint not required to answer the research question.

User Story 4 (Compute Feasibility and Resource Management) adds a fallback‑sampling mechanism and explicit resource‑monitoring logic. The idea’s methodology sketch contains no such resource‑management story, so this introduces new work not requested by the original research plan.

FR-010 requires the proportion of total R² attributable to pairwise interaction terms on an independent external hold‑out set to be ≥ 70 %. The idea only states an expectation that interactions explain >70 % of variance; it does not define the metric as a proportion of total R² nor tie it to an external hold‑out set. This redefines the evaluation criterion.

FR-002 specifies that models must be trained on the log₁₀‑transformed diffusion coefficient. The idea’s methodology sketch mentions training XGBoost and Random Forest regressors but never required a log‑scale transformation, so this adds an unrequested preprocessing step.
FR-006 also imposes a hard wall‑clock limit of 6 hours and a RAM ceiling of ~7 GB, plus a sampled‑subset fallback. These limits are not part of the original idea and constitute scope creep.
